answers.U1-S1: A boy goes on a long walk with his brother to a river and sees many birds, including three tall white-and-rose birds with crimson wings.
answers.U1-S2: He was terrified of the half-wild cattle they might meet on the walk.
answers.U1-S3: Because they had to take many turns to avoid the thistles, and the tall grass full of flowers was tiring to walk through.
answers.U1-S4: In a row, a yard or so apart from each other.
answers.U1-S5: Because when the wings were open they were a glorious crimson colour.
answers.U1-S6: They had never seen birds like them before.
answers.U1-S7: Because its wings were a glorious crimson colour when it opened them, and it was white and rose coloured.
answers.U1-S8: He says the delight in those spectacles never equalled what he felt when he was six years old.
answers.U1-S9: It tells how he saw the flamingo many more times later, at sunset, in the morning, and flying in flocks.
answers.U1-S10: He remembers it as the time he was amazed and enchanted by the birds, a delight never equalled.
